poc_summary: svg-alloc.ttf (a TrueType font with a gzip-compressed OT-SVG document table whose gzip trailer ISIZE field claims an uncompressed size of 128 MiB) is loaded via a custom oracle.c harness that calls FT_Init_FreeType/FT_New_Memory_Face/FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes/FT_Load_Glyph on the embedded SVG glyph, instrumented to intercept allocator calls and report the count/size of any allocation >= a large threshold.
explanation: Ran the identical oracle binary (built fresh against each revision's libfreetype.a per run.sh) against the identical svg-alloc.ttf input on pre_intro, post_intro, and post_benign. Results cleanly match the labelled regression: pre_intro reports large_alloc_count=0 (the glyph loader did not yet call tt_face_load_svg_doc at all prior to the intro commit, so the vulnerable path is unreached), post_intro reports large_alloc_count=1 max_large_bytes=134217728 (the newly-added call path reaches tt_face_load_svg_doc, which trusts the gzip trailer's ISIZE and requests an uncapped 128 MiB buffer via FT_QALLOC), and post_benign reports large_alloc_count=0 again (the companion fix caps the buffer size, matching upstream commit 6fa8725a4167's MAX_SVG_SIZE guard). This is a behavioral/logic oracle (no crash expected or required) measuring an unchecked oversized-allocation request, which is a faithful proxy for the documented allocation-bomb root cause. Same input/command invariant across all three builds.

oracle.description: Custom oracle.c harness loads the SVG glyph and instruments/intercepts the allocator to count and size-track any allocation requests at or above a large-size threshold while loading the embedded compressed OT-SVG document; run.sh classifies the oracle's printed summary line into VULNERABLE_128M_ALLOCATION_REQUEST vs NO_LARGE_ALLOCATION_REQUEST vs UNKNOWN and sets the process exit code accordingly.
oracle.target_evidence: run_poc(pre_intro): exit=0, output contains large_alloc_count=0 max_large_bytes=0, ORACLE_RESULT=NO_LARGE_ALLOCATION_REQUEST. run_poc(post_intro): exit=1, output contains large_alloc_count=1 max_large_bytes=134217728, ORACLE_RESULT=VULNERABLE_128M_ALLOCATION_REQUEST. run_poc(post_benign): exit=0, output contains large_alloc_count=0 max_large_bytes=0, ORACLE_RESULT=NO_LARGE_ALLOCATION_REQUEST. All three builds succeeded (build_ok=true) and used the identical input svg-alloc.ttf and identical run.sh/oracle.c invocation.
